title: SpecRecord
description: Any OpenAudit spec record. Optional fields are left out, never null. Ids are UUIDv7.

CommitmentCategory.title: CommitmentCategory
CommitmentCategory.description: `oversight`: outside people test or check the organization. `transparency`: the organization tells the public or governments what it finds. `limits`: the organization limits or stops its own development. `security`: it protects its models, or gives resources to safety.

CommitmentCriterion.title: CommitmentCriterion
CommitmentCriterion.description: One part of the ideal form of a commitment.

label.description: A few words in Title Case (`Deep Access`).

description.description: One sentence that tells what meets the criterion.

Commitment.title: Commitment
Commitment.description: One kind of safety commitment, with the criteria of its ideal form. Its page is `/organizations/commitments/<slug>`.

order.description: The place of the column in the table.

summary.description: One sentence that tells the ideal form.

description.description: Why it matters for safety, in 2 or 3 short sentences.

CommitmentLevel.title: CommitmentLevel
CommitmentLevel.description: How far the organization has committed. `full`: it meets all criteria, each independently verified. `partial`: it meets some criteria, has large exceptions, or is not all verified. `intent`: it says it will, with no terms or date. `none_found`: we checked and found no public commitment. `declined`: it publicly refused. `dropped`: it had the commitment, then withdrew it or let it end. `broken`: credible sources report that it did not keep the commitment.

CommitmentStrength.title: CommitmentStrength
CommitmentStrength.description: How enforceable the commitment is. `statement`: a post or a talk; it can change at any time. `policy`: in a published policy or framework with a change process. `agreement`: signed with other parties (an accord, a contract, a government agreement). `law`: a law or regulation requires it.

CommitmentDuration.title: CommitmentDuration
CommitmentDuration.description: `ongoing`: no end date. `time_limited`: a pilot, or a term with an end date.

CommitmentState.title: CommitmentState
CommitmentState.description: An organization's commitment at one time.

condition.description: The condition that the commitment depends on, in a few words (`If all frontier labs agree`). Empty when it has no condition.

criteria.description: Each criterion of the commitment by its key. A criterion that is not here is not known.

verified.description: The keys of the met or partly met criteria that an independent party can check, with a public result. Missing is none.

notes.description: Where the organization is now on each criterion, by its key.

limits.description: The exceptions and limits, each in a few words (`Lab can redact`).

CriterionNote.title: CriterionNote
CriterionNote.description: One criterion's state in short words. Each part is a phrase or one short sentence.

commitment.description: What the organization commits to or does for the criterion.

missing.description: What is missing for the criterion to be met and independently verified.

CommitmentQuote.title: CommitmentQuote
CommitmentQuote.description: The organization's own words, copied exactly from the source.

OrgCommitment.title: OrgCommitment
OrgCommitment.description: One organization's current state for one commitment: the state after its newest event, or `none_found` with no events. Its page is `/<organization slug>/commitments/<commitment slug>`.

checkedAt.description: The day of the newest research (YYYY-MM-DD).

checkedBy.description: The model that did the newest research, with its effort, as "Claude Opus 5.5 (High)".

summary.description: The current state in one sentence, for the table and the lists.

CommitmentEventKind.title: CommitmentEventKind
CommitmentEventKind.description: `announced`: the first commitment. `expanded` or `narrowed`: the terms changed. `renewed`: a time-limited commitment continued. `expired`: it ended at its end date. `withdrawn`: the organization dropped it. `broken`: sources report that it was not kept. `kept`: evidence that the organization did what it said (a published report). `declined`: the organization refused.

OrgCommitmentEvent.title: OrgCommitmentEvent
OrgCommitmentEvent.description: One event in an organization's commitment timeline, with the state after it.

order.description: The place in the timeline, from 0, oldest first.

title.description: A short headline (`Signs agreements with four embedded assessors`).

agreement.description: The shared agreement that the event is part of (`Frontier AI Safety Commitments`).

Id.title: Id
Id.description: A UUIDv7, made by the client that creates the record. Lowercase, with dashes.

Slug.title: Slug
Slug.description: A lowercase name for URLs and lookups (`google`, `01-ai`).

DocumentKey.title: DocumentKey
DocumentKey.description: A lowercase key for a document (`openai-gpt2-blog`).

PartialDate.title: PartialDate
PartialDate.description: A date only as exact as its source says (YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD).

Timestamp.title: Timestamp
Timestamp.description: An RFC 3339 time with a time zone.

Aliases.title: Aliases
Aliases.description: Other names for the record, for search and for matching names in documents.

DeployVerdict.title: DeployVerdict
DeployVerdict.description: What a Deploymeter score says about wide public deployment. `approve`: 70 to 100, wide use with normal safeguards or as it is. `limits`: 50 to 69, only with more safeguards or monitoring. `reject`: 0 to 49, limited use only, or not for wide use.

DeployReviewSample.title: DeployReviewSample
DeployReviewSample.description: One answer of a judge to the evidence packet. A review has more than one.

score.description: Trust for wide public deployment, from a safety view. A multiple of 5. When the judge abstains, the score it would give; it does not count.

abstain.description: True when the judge cannot give a fair score from the packet.

enoughEvidence.description: False when the judge found the packet too thin to judge. Only in older panels.

headline.description: The main point for a general reader, in one sentence.

reasoning.description: The reasoning that the provider shows: full text, or a summary for some providers. Null when it shows none.

DeployGuess.title: DeployGuess
DeployGuess.description: After its review, a judge guesses who made the model and which model it is. It shows how well the packet hides them. `rightDeveloper`: the guess names the developer.

reasoning.description: The reasoning that the provider shows for the guess, as in `DeployReviewSample`.

DeployPanelSummary.title: DeployPanelSummary
DeployPanelSummary.description: What the panel's reviews say together, written by one model from the reviews that count.

DocumentKind.title: DocumentKind
DocumentKind.description: What the document is. A system card and a safety report state the lab's tests. A model page is a short page about a model (specs and use), with no safety tests.

Document.title: Document
Document.description: A document an organization published about models: a link, our saved copy of the file and facts we took from it. `url` stays the publisher's link.

fileUrl.description: Where we got the saved copy, when it is not `url` (the PDF that a web page links to).

fileKey.description: The saved copy in our storage (`documents/<key>.pdf`).

sha256.description: The hash of the saved copy.

fetchedAt.description: When we fetched the saved copy.

verified.description: A person checked that the link works and that the publisher is correct.

notes.description: Notes for reviewers. Not shown on public pages.

Visibility.title: Visibility
Visibility.description: `private`: the owner only. `unlisted`: anyone with the link; never listed or indexed. `public`: listed and indexed. A record is never more visible than its parent.

EvalAccess.title: EvalAccess
EvalAccess.description: Who can get the samples. `public`: anyone. `gated`: after agreeing to the source's terms. `held_out`: kept back by the maintainer. `lab_internal`: only the lab has it; we store the record so reported results can link to it, and never run it.

EvalStatus.title: EvalStatus
EvalStatus.description: `active`: current, and we recommend it. `saturated`: valid, but current models score at the ceiling or the floor. `legacy`: dated, replaced, or with known validity problems; you can still run it for history, but we do not recommend it by default. `retired`: withdrawn; do not run it.

Measures.title: Measures
Measures.description: `capability`: can the subject do it. `propensity`: does it tend to. `robustness`: can its safeguards be broken.

EvalCases.title: EvalCases
EvalCases.description: `fixed`: a dataset. `generated`: an auditor model writes the conversation from a seed. `live_human`: people talk to the subject.

SubjectKind.title: SubjectKind
SubjectKind.description: What a run tests. `model`: a model. `auditor`: an agent (model, tools, scaffold) that audits target models. `method`: an interp method on a model, with its artifact (SAE, vector, probe).

Topic.title: Topic
Topic.description: What an eval is about. The same list tags system-card coverage.

EvalFacets.title: EvalFacets
EvalFacets.description: Independent answers to one question each. Labels such as "benchmark" or "red team" are combinations of these.

adversarial.description: The eval tries to make the subject fail (red teaming, jailbreaks).

humanParticipants.description: People take part, as in uplift trials.

EvalMaintainer.title: EvalMaintainer
EvalMaintainer.description: Who maintains the eval. Give `organizationId` when the maintainer is an `Organization`.

RecommendedModel.title: RecommendedModel
RecommendedModel.description: A model we recommend for one role in an eval, in place of its default. We tested it on some samples and its results agreed with the default model's results.

role.description: The role, as the eval's task names it (`judge`, `auditor`, `grader`).

model.description: The model, as OpenRouter names it (`google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite`).

recommendedAt.description: The day we made the recommendation (YYYY-MM-DD).

replaces.description: The default model for the role (`openai/gpt-4-turbo`).

version.description: The eval version that we tested.

evidence.description: Markdown. What we tested (samples, agreement, cost) and the run ids.

EvalLinkKind.title: EvalLinkKind
EvalLinkKind.description: `hf_benchmark`: a Hugging Face benchmark dataset repo, for Community Evals. `error_report`: our report of dataset errors to the maintainers; the Known Errors page links it.

EvalSuite.title: EvalSuite
EvalSuite.description: A set of evals that one source publishes together (SAEBench). Its page compares method variants across its evals. An eval names its suite with `suiteId`.

summary.description: One plain sentence about what the suite tests.

evalOrder.description: Slugs of its evals in display order, safety tasks first. Its other evals follow, safety tasks first, then by name.

matched.description: Compare method variants at set values of one metric of a suite eval. Without it, each variant uses its one artifact in a group.

Eval.title: Eval
Eval.description: A test of models, auditors or interp methods: a benchmark, a red team, an automated audit. Results point to one of its `EvalVersion`s.

slug.description: The name in URLs (`petri`, `mask`). Unique on the site.

aliases.description: Other spellings in documents (`Model Alignment between Statements and Knowledge`).

summary.description: One plain sentence about what the eval tests, for lists and tables ("Tests whether the model lies under pressure about what it believes is true.").

family.description: Groups related evals (`Petri` for Petri and Petri Bloom suites).

suiteId.description: The `EvalSuite` that the eval is part of.

saturatedReason.description: One line on why we marked it `saturated` (`Current models refuse almost every prompt.`). Markdown.

legacyReason.description: One line on why we marked it `legacy` (`Built for base-model continuation; chat models score near zero.`). Markdown.

supersededBy.description: The slug of the newer eval to use in place of this one.

autoApprove.description: A full run costs little, so a user's request of it starts without an admin's approval (when its estimated cost is under the limit).

recommendedModels.description: Cheaper judge or helper models that we tested against the defaults.

canary.description: The eval's canary string. We show it on each page, so training filters can drop them.

ownerUserId.description: The user who made it. Left out for evals in the site registry (seed data).

visibility.description: A private eval needs an owner. Anyone with the link can open an unlisted eval.

EvalVersionStatus.title: EvalVersionStatus
EvalVersionStatus.description: `draft`: can change. `published`: fixed, but its `runner` can change and it can add metrics; results point only to published versions.

SampleStorage.title: SampleStorage
SampleStorage.description: `stored`: we keep the samples (the license allows it). `pointer`: a link to the source revision, and each sample's id and hash. `hash_only`: only a hash of each sample (held out).

name.description: The split name in the source (`test`, `public`, `private`).

EvalDataset.title: EvalDataset
EvalDataset.description: Where the samples come from. Give `hfRepo` and `revision`, or `url`.

revision.description: The commit or tag the samples come from.

sha256.description: The hash of all samples in order, as the spec serializes them.

license.description: An SPDX id when there is one (`cc-by-4.0`), else the license name.

sources.description: More data the task loads, for suites that join datasets (AbstentionBench).

DatasetSource.title: DatasetSource
DatasetSource.description: One more place a task loads data from. Give `hfRepo` and `revision`, or `url`.

url.description: A file at a pinned commit (a GitHub raw URL).

DisplayRule.title: DisplayRule
DisplayRule.description: Who can read sample text: inputs, targets, transcripts and logs. `open`: anyone. `sign_in`: signed-in users who accepted the dataset's terms on our site. `scores_only`: nobody; pages show only scores and pass or fail.

SubsetTerms.title: SubsetTerms
SubsetTerms.description: A rule for the samples whose metadata `key` equals `value` (a dataset inside a suite).

key.description: The sample metadata key, as the Inspect task sets it (`dataset_name`).

quote.description: The terms, as the source states them.

SampleTerms.title: SampleTerms
SampleTerms.description: The source's terms on showing its samples, and our rule for them. Left out: `open`.

quote.description: The terms, as the source states them. Left out when the source states none.

source.description: Where the terms are (the gate page or the README).

note.description: Why this rule, when the quote alone does not say.

subsets.description: Rules for some samples. A matching rule replaces `display` for those samples.

ScoreType.title: ScoreType
ScoreType.description: `binary`: 0 or 1 (pass). `ordinal`: whole steps from `min` to `max` (a 1-10 judge scale). `continuous`: any number, in `[min, max]` when given.

Direction.title: Direction
Direction.description: `nearer_zero_is_better`: a signed number where 0 is best and both signs are worse.

ScoreDef.title: ScoreDef
ScoreDef.description: One score a scorer gives each attempt (Petri's judge gives about 36).

attemptName.description: The name of this score on an attempt when it is not `key` or ends with `/<key>`, such as the scorer's name (`fortress_scorer_adversarial`).

attemptScale.description: The factor that puts an attempt's value on this score's scale (100 for a 0 to 1 value of a percent).

description.description: What the score means; for a judge, a summary of its rubric.

PassRule.title: PassRule
PassRule.description: When one attempt's value of this score is a pass or a fail, if the direction cannot tell. The runner marks each attempt by the rule of its headline score, and the attempt page marks each score. With no rule, the direction decides: see `ADD_AN_EVAL.md`. A value that the rule does not name has no mark.

values.description: Each value as text and its mark: true for a pass (MASK: `honest` true, `lie` false). Case and spaces at the ends do not count. A number is its shortest text (`1`, `0.5`).

byTarget.description: For each sample target, the values and their marks, as in `values` (AbstentionBench: with the target `True`, `yes` is a pass).

failAtOrAbove.description: A number at this value or above is a fail, and a lower number is a pass (Petri's 1 to 10 scale, 7).

groups.description: The group metric keys that the rule is for. An attempt in none of them has no mark (APE: only the harmful topics).

none.description: No mark on any value, for a score that is not good or bad for safety by itself.

MetricAggregation.title: MetricAggregation
MetricAggregation.description: How attempts become one number. `mean`: the mean of a score. `rate`: the share of attempts whose binary score is 1. `pass_at_k`: pass@k over trials. `custom`: the eval's own formula (see `description`).

MetricDef.title: MetricDef
MetricDef.description: One aggregate number an `EvalResult` can hold.

score.description: The `ScoreDef.key` it comes from. Left out for `custom`.

unit.description: Left out for a plain number or a fraction (`percent`, `tokens`).

direction.description: Which way is better for the eval's own goal. For a skill eval, more skill.

safetyDirection.description: Which way is better for safety, as in `EvalResult.safetyDirection`; measured results get it. `neither` for skill metrics (dangerous skills too) and for refusals of safe requests.

headline.description: The number to show first. At most one per version.

ModelRole.title: ModelRole
ModelRole.description: A model's part in a run, as Inspect's `model_roles`. `target`: the model under test. `auditor`: writes the other side of the conversation. `judge`: scores. `monitor`: watches the target for bad actions. `generator`: writes samples.

ModelSlot.title: ModelSlot
ModelSlot.description: One model a task needs besides the target. The runner gives it as `taskArg` or as `inspectRole`; give one. A run can change it; a re-score can change it only when `scoring`.

label.description: The name to show (`Refusal judge`). Default from `id`.

taskArg.description: Give the model as this task argument (`scorer_model`).

index.description: The place in a list task argument (`grader_models`).

inspectRole.description: Give the model as this Inspect model role (`grader`).

default.description: The model the task uses when not told, as a route model id (`openai/gpt-4o`). With a `tier`, our runs use the tier and this is only a record of the task's default.

tier.description: The lowest tier in spec/model-ladders.yaml that is good enough for this slot. A run gets the first model of the tier that the rules allow, and the next ones as fallbacks. A model of a higher tier is also good enough.

labs.description: Use these labs' models of the tier first, in this order, when the rules allow it.

sameLab.description: The slot can use a model of the target's lab (one judge in a panel of judges from several labs). It never uses the target model itself.

scoring.description: Only the scorer uses it, so a re-score can change it.

RunnerKind.title: RunnerKind
RunnerKind.description: `inspect`: an Inspect task. `openaudit`: our runner. `external`: the maintainer's own code.

EvalRunner.title: EvalRunner
EvalRunner.description: How to run a version. Optional; a run can come from anywhere.

package.description: The package and version that has the task (`inspect-evals==0.9.2`).

dependencies.description: Other packages the task uses, each with its version (`inspect-petri==3.1.0`).

roles.description: The model roles a run must fill.

models.description: The models besides the target, and how the task gets each one.

targetRole.description: Also give the target as this Inspect model role (`target`), for tasks that read it by role.

sandbox.description: The sandbox the task needs (`docker`), if any.

gpu.description: The runner needs a GPU (white-box methods).

rawReasoning.description: The scores need the model's raw chain of thought. Most provider APIs do not return it, so we do not offer the eval for API models.

defaultLimit.description: The samples a run does when its settings give no limit. A run with this limit or more counts as a full run.

EvalVersion.title: EvalVersion
EvalVersion.description: One fixed form of an eval: its samples and how they are scored. Results from different versions are not comparable. A new version when the samples, scores, rubric or task defaults change. Judge and auditor models are run settings. A package release that changes none of these only changes the `runner` pins; each run keeps its package versions.

version.description: The maintainer's name for it (`2.0`, `2026-02`). Unique per eval.

changes.description: What changed from the version before, in Markdown.

methodSetup.description: Only for evals whose subjects are methods.

subject.description: The Hub name of the subject model, as artifacts give it.

SubjectOrder.title: SubjectOrder
SubjectOrder.description: A number for each subject model that sorts the leaderboard rows (a capability index).

MethodEvalSetup.title: MethodEvalSetup
MethodEvalSetup.description: How an eval of tools defines its positive cases and sets thresholds.

definition.description: Markdown. What counts as a positive case (a lie).

calibration.description: Markdown. How each tool sets its threshold before it is scored.

coreSubjects.description: The subject models that rank the variants. A variant needs a result on each to have a rank.

ResultSettings.title: ResultSettings
ResultSettings.description: How the number was made. Compare results only when these match. Left out: not stated.

helpfulOnly.description: A helpful-only model, without safety training.

otherModels.description: The judge and other models besides the target, as `slot: model` pairs (`judge: openai/gpt-4o`). Scores with different judges are not comparable.

other.description: Anything else the source says about the setup.

page.description: The page or section, as printed in the document.

pdfPage.description: The page in the document's saved PDF, from 1. Links go here.

EvalResult.title: EvalResult
EvalResult.description: One number: one metric of one eval for one model. A reported result that matches no `Eval` or `Model` yet keeps the raw name, and the id is added later.

rawEvalName.description: The eval's name as the source writes it (`SWE-bench Verified (n=500)`).

rawModelName.description: The model's name as the source writes it.

metric.description: A `MetricDef.key` when the version is known; else the source's words.

unit.description: `percent` is 0-100 and `fraction` is 0-1. `score` is any other scale.

n.description: The number of samples, when stated.

safetyDirection.description: Which way is better for safety. `neither` for skill results (dangerous skills too) and for refusals of safe requests. Left out: not known.

capabilityDirection.description: Which way shows more skill. `neither` for behavior results. Left out: not known.

evalRunId.description: The run a `measured` result comes from.

RunStatus.title: RunStatus
RunStatus.description: `requested`: a user asked for it; it waits for an admin to approve it. `queued`: waits for a runner. `running`: a runner has it. `importing`: the log is being saved. `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`: done.

RunOrigin.title: RunOrigin
RunOrigin.description: `run`: our runner ran it. `import`: a log made elsewhere, imported. `rescore`: our runner scored the outputs of `sourceRunId` again, with other scoring models.

RouteKind.title: RouteKind
RouteKind.description: How the target model was served. `direct`: the lab's own API. `openrouter`, `bedrock`, `vertex`, `azure`: that router or cloud. `engine`: our interp-engine server.

ServingRoute.title: ServingRoute
ServingRoute.description: How a run reached the model. Provenance and a filter; not a change to the model.

model.description: The model id on the route (`qwen/qwen3.6-27b`).

providers.description: The providers the router may use, in order (OpenRouter `provider.order`).

fallbacks.description: For a slot: other models to try, in order, when this model fails a call or refuses it (an error, a content filter or an empty reply).

quantization.description: The weights' precision as the route states it (`bf16`, `fp8`, `unknown`).

RunSettings.title: RunSettings
RunSettings.description: What the runner was asked to do. Left out: the task's default.

reasoning.description: Thinking effort, in OpenRouter's words. `none`: no thinking. `on`: thinking at the model's default, for models with no effort levels.

limit.description: Run only the first samples of the dataset.

maxConnections.description: Parallel model calls in each shard.

shardSize.description: Samples in each shard. Left out, the runner's default.

capKey.description: The `runner_cap` key for the run's shards, for one cap per model server. Left out: from the route.

models.description: The model for each slot in the version's `runner.models`, by slot id.

cacheRead.description: Input tokens read from the provider's prompt cache. Part of `input`.

cacheWrite.description: Input tokens written to the provider's prompt cache. Part of `input`.

FileRef.title: FileRef
FileRef.description: A file in our private storage.

RunProvenance.title: RunProvenance
RunProvenance.description: Where and how the run happened.

tool.description: The program that ran the eval (`inspect_ai`).

packages.description: Package versions, as the log states them (`{"inspect_evals": "0.22.0"}`).

task.description: The task as the log names it (`inspect_evals/truthfulqa`).

logModel.description: The model as the log names it (`openrouter/qwen/qwen3.6-27b`).

servedBy.description: The providers that served the model calls, as the route reported them.

host.description: The machine the runner ran on.

costUsd.description: What this run paid, when the routes say. A re-score pays only its judges.

note.description: What a reader must know about an imported run, from the log (`eval.metadata.note`). The run and attempt pages show it.

byModel.description: Tokens and cost for each model, by the name in the log.

byRole.description: Tokens and cost for each model role (`target`, `auditor`, `judge`, `judge_2`). A re-score has only its judges.

erroredSamples.description: Samples with an error and no score. The results leave them out.

fallbacks.description: The calls that a slot's fallback models made in place of its model.

blocks.description: Model calls that a provider refused for its policy, by provider. A run that failed or was cancelled because of a block also has them.

ProviderBlock.title: ProviderBlock
ProviderBlock.description: Samples whose model calls a provider refused for its policy (not the model's own refusal). These samples have no score.

kind.description: `account`: the provider blocked our account, so it refuses all calls. `content`: it refused these prompts only.

model.description: The model of the refused calls, when the error names it.

samples.description: The samples with this block. Zero when the run stopped before its samples.

costEstimated.description: The route did not state the cost; `costUsd` is list price times tokens.

EvalRun.title: EvalRun
EvalRun.description: One run of an eval version on one model, with its settings and provenance. `measured` results and attempts point to it.

sourceRunId.description: For a re-score, the run whose outputs it scores.

sampleCount.description: The samples the run plans to do.

AttemptScore.title: AttemptScore
AttemptScore.description: One scorer's grade of an attempt, as Inspect's `Score`.

value.description: A number, a letter (`C` correct, `I` incorrect), or a yes/no.

answer.description: The answer the scorer read from the output.

Hazard.title: Hazard
Hazard.description: Who can read a reply that can give dangerous help. `gated`: anyone, but no public share (J-Lens). `restricted`: staff. `withheld`: nobody on the site. The prompt, target and scores stay open.

EvalAttempt.title: EvalAttempt
EvalAttempt.description: One sample in one epoch of a run: a short copy of the input and output for lists, the scores, and the full transcript in `body`.

ordinal.description: The attempt's place in the log, from 1. URLs use it.

sampleId.description: The sample's id in the log.

evalSampleId.description: The stored `EvalSample`, when we keep the samples.

passed.description: The headline score is correct. Left out when the score is not pass or fail.

metrics.description: The keys of the metrics over a part of the samples (a category or group) that count this attempt, such as `harm_score_copyright`.

notScored.description: Why the attempt has no scores, from the sample's `notScored` metadata.

display.description: A subset rule that matched this sample. Left out, the version's rule applies.

hazard.description: Set from the dataset's labels when the eval graded the reply unsafe. Left out, open.

SampleMessage.title: SampleMessage
SampleMessage.description: One chat message of a sample's input. Text only.

EvalSample.title: EvalSample
EvalSample.description: One sample of an eval version, as Inspect's `Sample`. Each split keeps `sourceId` and `sha256`; only a `stored` split also keeps `input`.

sourceId.description: The sample's id in the source. Unique in its split.

target.description: The answer or answers the scorer looks for.

choices.description: The options of a multiple-choice sample.

metadata.description: Other fields of the source sample, as they are in the source.

sha256.description: The hash of `{"id": sourceId, "input": input}` as JSON with sorted keys and no spaces. Chat input is `SampleMessage[]`.

MethodGroup.title: MethodGroup
MethodGroup.description: What the method reads. `white_box`: activations, weights or token log probs (it needs model access). `black_box`: only text. Topics, not groups, tell the job of a method.

ExpertStance.title: ExpertStance
ExpertStance.description: What a view says about its method, on balance.

text.description: The words of the source, unchanged.

MethodAccess.title: MethodAccess
MethodAccess.description: What a variant needs from the subject model. `white_box`: activations or weights. `logprobs`: token log probabilities only. `black_box`: text in and out only.

MethodParam.title: MethodParam
MethodParam.description: One setting that artifacts of a method can have (`width`, `judgeModel`). A key keeps its meaning for all variants of the method.

MethodMatch.title: MethodMatch
MethodMatch.description: Compare variants at set values of one metric (SAEs at the same L0). A value between the points of a variant is interpolated.

eval.description: The eval that gives the metric.

MethodCompare.title: MethodCompare
MethodCompare.description: How to compare the variants of a method. Artifacts compete only when they have the same subject and the same value for each `groupBy` key. The `matched` rule of an `EvalSuite` tells how to compare on its evals.

Method.title: Method
Method.description: A kind of tool that does a set of jobs (sparse autoencoders, probes, LLM monitors). The method page tells which safety use the evals test.

summary.description: One sentence. What the method does.

tagline.description: A few words for lists, next to the name: what the method does (`Read what a model has in mind, as words.`).

safetyUse.description: Markdown. The safety jobs the method could do, and which evals test them.

caveats.description: Markdown. Limits a reader must know before comparing variants.

params.description: The settings that its artifacts can have.

expertSummary.description: What the expert views say on balance: where they agree and where they disagree. Plain words, 50 words or fewer, with no names and no links.

MethodVariant.title: MethodVariant
MethodVariant.description: One recipe or architecture of a method (TopK SAE, Apollo probe). A `baseline` is a simple reference that a variant must beat (raw activations, PCA). A changed recipe is a new variant, with `supersedesId` set to the old one.

componentIds.description: The variants that this one combines (a probe that reads SAE latents).

supersedesId.description: The variant that this one replaces.

params.description: Settings of this variant only, added to those of its method.

prompts.description: The prompts of a variant that is an LLM, as the judge prompt of a monitor.

visibility.description: Left out, `public`. Anyone with the link can open an unlisted variant.

MethodPrompt.title: MethodPrompt
MethodPrompt.description: One prompt of a variant, word for word.

name.description: What the prompt is for (`Judge prompt`).

text.description: The prompt. A `{name}` part is filled in for each call.

note.description: How the filled-in parts are made, for example the format of the transcript.

MethodExpertView.title: MethodExpertView
MethodExpertView.description: What human experts said about a method, from one public source (a post or paper), with its nuance. The summary and points are ours; quotes are the source's words. A source about two methods has one view in each.

variantIds.description: The variants of the method that the source names.

title.description: Our plain headline for the view.

byline.description: The authors as the source lists them, short (`Lewis Smith, Neel Nanda and 6 others`).

summary.description: Markdown. What the source found and concluded, in plain words.

points.description: Markdown. The nuance and limits that the source gives.

sources.description: The original first, then copies and companion posts.

MethodSite.title: MethodSite
MethodSite.description: One place in the subject model where an artifact reads or writes.

address.description: The interp-engine address of the point (`resid_post.12`, `resid_post.5.stream-2`). Left out when the source does not say which point it uses.

source.description: The name that the source uses (`blocks.12.hook_resid_post`, `layer 58`).

MethodArtifact.title: MethodArtifact
MethodArtifact.description: One trained SAE or probe, or one monitor setup, for one subject model. Evals score artifacts, not variants.

key.description: A stable key from the source (`gemma-2-2b/l12/w16k/topk/trainer-2`).

subject.description: The model that the artifact inspects, as its Hub name (`google/gemma-2-2b`), or the name of a synthetic model.

modelId.description: The `Model`, when the subject is in the catalog.

revision.description: The Hub revision of the subject.

sites.description: Empty for a variant that does not use activations.

params.description: Values for the `MethodParam` keys of the method and variant.

sourceUrl.description: Where to get the weights or the setup.

files.description: The files to download, as the weights of a probe. Each has a `url`, a `mirror`, or both.

url.description: The file at its source, at a fixed commit.

mirror.description: The key of our copy in R2. `apps/web/scripts/mirror-artifact-files.ts` uploads the file and sets it.

MethodResult.title: MethodResult
MethodResult.description: One number for one artifact on one eval version, as the source gives it.

metric.description: A `MetricDef` key of the eval version.

sourceCommit.description: The commit of the eval code that made the number.

ModelSource.title: ModelSource
ModelSource.description: `hf`: weights on the Hugging Face Hub (or `local/<name>`). `api`: a model behind a provider API. The name alone can collide (`openai/gpt-oss-20b` is open), so the source is part of the identity.

ParentRelation.title: ParentRelation
ParentRelation.description: How a model comes from its parent, as the Hub's `base_model:<relation>:` tags.

Model.title: Model
Model.description: One model. Its facts are here, each with a source; a document is one source.

name.description: The HF repo id or `local/<name>` for `hf`; `provider/model` for `api`. Unique with `source`. Also the URL path.

revision.description: The HF commit or the API snapshot id that the facts refer to.

aliases.description: Other names, such as API ids (`davinci`) and old names.

parentId.description: The model this one comes from. One parent; a chain for combinations.

removedFromHub.description: The Hub repo was removed or made private. We keep the record.

pretrained.description: A base model: pretrained only, with no instruct or chat tuning. Lists do not show it.

documentIds.description: The `Document`s about this model. The order has no meaning.

ModelFacts.title: ModelFacts
ModelFacts.description: Facts about a model. A fact is left out when nobody has found it yet.

reasoningModes.description: The reasoning settings the model has (`none`, `low`, `high`).

license.description: An SPDX id when there is one (`apache-2.0`), else the license name.

activeParams.description: Parameters used per token. Less than `totalParams` for a mixture of experts.

kind.description: `document`: a `Document` (give `documentId`, and `page` and `quote` when you can). `hf_config`: the model's Hub config. `provider_docs` and `url`: a web page (give `url`). `manual`: entered by a person without a source to cite.

ModelLadders.title: ModelLadders
ModelLadders.description: The default models for the LLM jobs that OpenAudit runs itself, from spec/model-ladders.yaml. A tier is a ladder of models of about the same quality and price from different labs, best first. A role uses a tier or its own list. For a target model, a role skips the models of the target's lab.

labs.description: Other name prefixes of a lab, to the prefix that the ladders use (`meta-llama` to `meta`).

openWeights.description: The models in the ladders that have open weights.

models.description: Best first. At most one model per lab, so that each target gets a model.

LadderRole.title: LadderRole
LadderRole.description: A job and its models. It has a `tier` or `models`, not both.

tier.description: The name of a tier in `tiers`.

models.description: The role's own ladder, best first, in place of a tier.

SystemicRisk.title: SystemicRisk
SystemicRisk.description: A specified systemic risk of the EU General-Purpose AI Code of Practice, Safety and Security chapter, Appendix 1.4. `cbrn`: chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear. `cyber_offence`: large-scale cyber-attacks. `loss_of_control`: people can no longer direct, change or shut down the model. `harmful_manipulation`: strategic distortion of beliefs or behavior of many people or of high-stakes decision-makers.

VerdictLevel.title: VerdictLevel
VerdictLevel.description: Our level for one risk, from our eval runs only. It is not the Code's risk tier and not a legal finding. `not_enough_evidence`: no eval run, or too few samples, covers the risk. `no_evidence`: the runs that cover the risk show no sign of it. `low`, `moderate`, `high`: the runs show signs of the risk, from small to strong.

CoverageLevel.title: CoverageLevel
CoverageLevel.description: How well our runs cover a topic or a risk. `none`, `weak` (few samples or one narrow eval), `some`, `good`.

CardFinding.title: CardFinding
CardFinding.description: One notable finding, in Markdown. It names the runs (and snippets) it rests on.

RiskVerdict.title: RiskVerdict
RiskVerdict.description: Our verdict on one systemic risk. `evidence` is the runs it rests on; `missing` says what no run covers yet.

summary.description: Markdown. What the evidence shows, and how strong it is.

missing.description: The parts of the risk that no run covers.

TopicSummary.title: TopicSummary
TopicSummary.description: What our runs show for one topic. `summary` is left out when no run covers it.

CoverageGap.title: CoverageGap
CoverageGap.description: A topic or a risk that our runs do not cover, or cover only weakly.

CardRun.title: CardRun
CardRun.description: One run a version used, and its eval version.

OpenAuditCardVersion.title: OpenAuditCardVersion
OpenAuditCardVersion.description: One version of a model's OpenAudit Card: our summary from our own eval runs only. An LLM (`aggregator`) writes it from the runs' results and the flagged snippets.

SnippetCategory.title: SnippetCategory
SnippetCategory.description: The topic (an eval `Topic`) of the AI's act, or `other`. Topics about the test, not an act in one transcript, are not in the list.

SnippetSeverity.title: SnippetSeverity
SnippetSeverity.description: `critical`: only from older flaggers. `high`: the AI seems willing to let people be killed or badly hurt, by real help or by a deliberate act as an agent. `medium`: other harmful help or acts, or a lie, hallucination or bias on something that matters. `low`: a small problem.

index.description: The message's place in the target's thread, from 0.

text.description: The message text, cut when long.

quote.description: The exact words that show the problem. Left out when the flagger's quote is not in the transcript.

OpenAuditSnippet.title: OpenAuditSnippet
OpenAuditSnippet.description: One case that the flagger model marked in one attempt of a run.

title.description: The problem in 1 to 3 words, for example "Copyright violation". Older snippets have none.

Organization.title: Organization
Organization.description: A lab or company that makes models or publishes documents.

slug.description: The organization's page URL (`/qwen`, `/google`): the model owner that most of its models use, in lowercase. Unique. Also a reserved handle.

aliases.description: Other names in documents (`Google DeepMind` and `Google Research` for `google`).

slugAliases.description: Other slugs that redirect to `slug`: old slugs and other model owners (`alibaba` for `qwen`). Unique across all organizations.

summary.description: 1 to 3 sentences about the organization, with inline source links.

researchedAt.description: The day of the newest research for the organization page (YYYY-MM-DD). New research looks only for events after this day.

researchDepth.description: How wide the research was. `deep`: many searches and primary sources. `light`: a few searches; empty lists are usual.

Markdown.title: Markdown
Markdown.description: Markdown text. Raw HTML is not shown.

DatePrecision.title: DatePrecision
DatePrecision.description: How exact the date next to it is. It agrees with the date's form (YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM, YYYY).

OrgSource.title: OrgSource
OrgSource.description: A public source for a fact.

IncidentSeverity.title: IncidentSeverity
IncidentSeverity.description: `red`: someone died, or many people were severely harmed, in credible reports or lawsuits. `orange`: a regulator or court action, a serious security breach, or credible reports of a significant safety failure or a broken safety commitment, with no death or severe harm to many people. `yellow`: concerning, but limited or disputed.

IncidentPrimaryCategory.title: IncidentPrimaryCategory
IncidentPrimaryCategory.description: What went wrong. `model_hacking`: a model broke into systems, took credentials or got out of its limits by itself. `model_deception`: a model lied, schemed or hid what it did. `model_misbehavior`: a model did other harmful things that nobody asked for. `suicide_and_delusion`: chats linked to suicide, self-harm or delusions. `sexual_content_with_minors`: sexual chats with minors, or child abuse images. `nonconsensual_images`: sexual or fake images of real people. `false_or_hateful_claims`: the model stated false information or hate. `used_by_attackers`: criminals or state actors used the model for attacks, targeting, influence operations or violence. `safeguards_failed`: the model gave dangerous help, or its safeguards were weak or off. `systems_breached`: attackers got into the organization's systems or accounts. `data_exposed`: the organization leaked user data, keys, code or weights. `prompt_injection`: a product flaw lets outside content control an agent. `privacy_violation`: the organization collected, used or uploaded data without clear consent. `safety_related_cut`: the organization dropped safety commitments, testing, reports, teams or staff.

IncidentLogRole.title: IncidentLogRole
IncidentLogRole.description: Who wrote a log step. `reasoning`: the model's thinking (chain of thought). `tool_call`: a command or tool call by the model. `tool_result`: what a tool or the environment returned. `note`: our short note between steps; it is not from the log.

label.description: The source's label for the step (`Tool result — Slack message`).

text.description: As the source shows it. `[...]` marks text that the source cut, and `[name]` text that it replaced.

IncidentLog.title: IncidentLog
IncidentLog.description: One excerpt of a log (a chat, chain of thought or tool calls) from a source, with the steps copied as the source shows them.

title.description: A few words about the excerpt (`The model reads the Slack thread`).

description.description: 1 or 2 short sentences about what the excerpt shows.

model.description: The model as the source names it.

ocr.description: The steps are read from a screenshot.

OrgIncident.title: OrgIncident
OrgIncident.description: A significant AI safety, security or responsible-AI event that involves the organization or its models, with at least one safety category. Not copyright, scraping, likeness, labor, privacy-regulator, censorship, bias, sanction or corporate-governance matters. Its page is `/<organization slug>/incidents/<slug>`.

primaryCategory.description: The one category that the feeds show.

description.description: 2 or 3 short sentences, on the incident page.

modelIds.description: The models whose behavior is the incident: the model that did the unsafe act, that people misused, or whose weights leaked or safeguard failed. Any developer. Empty when no model's behavior is part of it. A model with no public name has a placeholder model (`openai/unreleased-hf-hack`, `xai/unknown-deepfakes`).

logs.description: Log excerpts that show the model's behavior, in source order.

OrgIncidentEvent.title: OrgIncidentEvent
OrgIncidentEvent.description: One event in an incident's timeline.

order.description: The place in the timeline, from 0. Events with the same date keep this order.

OrgDeparture.title: OrgDeparture
OrgDeparture.description: A person who left in 2023 or later over AI safety concerns at the organization, or a safety leader who left. Not ethics, copyright or personal reasons.

title.description: The person's role at the organization.

quote.description: The person's own words, copied exactly from the source.

image.description: A freely licensed photo from Wikimedia Commons.

author.description: The author as Commons states it.

CardSource.title: CardSource
CardSource.description: Where in the document a value is. The quote is the card's own words.

page.description: The page or section (`12`, `5.3.2`), as printed in the document.

pdfPage.description: The page in our saved PDF, from 1. Links go here; `page` is what we show.

Disclosure.title: Disclosure
Disclosure.description: One model fact. `stated`: the card says it (give `value` and `source`). `not_stated`: we read the card; it does not say. Left out: not extracted yet.

value.description: The value in the card's words (`200K tokens`, `March 2026`).

Disclosures.title: Disclosures
Disclosures.description: The disclosure checklist. The keys match `ModelFacts`, plus training facts.

RiskLevel.title: RiskLevel
RiskLevel.description: Our coarse level, for sorting only. Always show the lab's own label next to it. `below`: under the lab's first threshold. `early_warning`: an alert or watch level. `reached`: a threshold is reached or cannot be ruled out. `highest`: the top level.

FrameworkId.title: FrameworkId
FrameworkId.description: A published safety framework. `anthropic-rsp`: Responsible Scaling Policy (also ASL levels). `anthropic-fcf`: Frontier Compliance Framework. `openai-preparedness`: Preparedness Framework. `google-fsf`: Frontier Safety Framework. `meta-aasf`: Advanced AI Scaling Framework. `amazon-fmsf`: Frontier Model Safety Framework. `xai-faif`: Frontier Artificial Intelligence Framework. `xai-rmf`: Risk Management Framework. `seoul-commitments`: Frontier AI Safety Commitments (Seoul, 2024).

RiskDecision.title: RiskDecision
RiskDecision.description: One risk decision the lab states for one domain.

frameworks.description: The published frameworks the verdict is made under. Leave out if none is named.

decidedBy.description: Who decided, when the card says (`Responsible Scaling Officer`).

modelIds.description: The covered models the verdict is about. Left out when it is about all of them.

TopicCoverage.title: TopicCoverage
TopicCoverage.description: Does the card cover a topic. `covered`: give a source, and a headline number when there is one. Not covered: the card has nothing on it. Left out: not extracted yet.

headline.description: The main result in the card's words (`0.8% jailbreak success`).

scope.description: What they tested (`autonomy and AI R&D`).

Finding.title: Finding
Finding.description: A notable finding that fits nowhere else. Short, in our words, with the quote.

FindingTone.title: FindingTone
FindingTone.description: Our reading for a safety reader. `good`: good for safety. `mixed`: mixed, a mild concern or an important caveat. `bad`: a clear concern. `neutral`: a fact or method note.

ExtractionInfo.title: ExtractionInfo
ExtractionInfo.description: How a record was made. `by` is the model or person.

CardCover.title: CardCover
CardCover.description: A model the card covers. `rawModelName` when the model is not in our list yet.

section.description: The section about it, for cards that cover several models (`Appendix B`).

SystemCard.title: SystemCard
SystemCard.description: What we extracted from one card. One card can have several documents (the PDF, the web page, the blog post); `documentId` is the one we read.

alsoDocumentIds.description: Other documents of the same card.

basedOnDocumentId.description: The card this one updates (a delta card).

reviewed.description: A person checked it. Pages mark unreviewed values "Not reviewed".

ReasoningKind.title: ReasoningKind
ReasoningKind.description: `raw`: the model's own thinking (open models). `summary`: the provider's summary. `omitted`: the provider gave none. `redacted`: the provider hid it.

signature.description: The provider's opaque blob, kept so the transcript can continue there.

OtherPart.title: OtherPart
OtherPart.description: A part we do not show yet (an image, audio); the original log keeps it.

Message.title: Message
Message.description: One chat message. A superset of Inspect's and OpenAI's shape.

id.description: Stable, so notes and links survive import and export.

toolCallId.description: For a `tool` message, the call it answers.

model.description: For an `assistant` message, the model that wrote it.

name.description: The model or person as the source names it.

Thread.title: Thread
Thread.description: One participant's ordered view of the conversation.

Transcript.title: Transcript
Transcript.description: The messages of one attempt or chat. Scores stay on the attempt. `extensions` keeps source fields we do not map (`extensions.inspect`).
